{"summary": "Localized the docs site's page metadata and social card generation:

1. **`docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts`** — exported a new `NON_LATIN_LOCALES` map (moved from `config.ts`'s `LOGO_VARIANT`), the set of locales whose script isn't covered by the bundled Latin webfont/wordmark.

2. **`docs/.vitepress/config.ts`** — the `og:description`/`twitter:description` were already per-locale, but `og:image`, `twitter:image`, `og:image:alt`, `twitter:image:alt`, and the `WebSite` JSON-LD script were static/English-only in the top-level `head` array (this is what caused `/hu/` to always show the English `description` in its structured data). Moved all of these into `transformHead` so every page emits locale-appropriate values: `websiteJsonLd()` now sets `description`/`inLanguage`/`url` from the resolved locale, and `ogImageUrl()` picks a per-locale card image for Latin-script locales.

3. **`docs/scripts/gen-og.ts`** — now reads each locale's own `hero.text`/`hero.tagline` from its `docs/{locale}/index.md` frontmatter (the same "homepage namespace" strings the home page itself renders) and renders a localized OG card per Latin-script locale (`og.png` for root, `og-<locale>.png` for the rest), with dynamic word-wrap/line-height and an SVG `textLength` fallback so translated text of any length fits the card. Non-Latin-script locales (already flagged via `NON_LATIN_LOCALES`, which also drives their bespoke wordmark logo) fall back to the English card, since the bundled font has no glyphs for those scripts.

Verified by running `node scripts/gen-og.ts` directly (generates 31 per-locale cards + the root card) and visually checking the Hungarian and Indonesian cards render correctly with wrapped, non-overlapping text; confirmed the pre-existing `tsc --noEmit` crash on this file is unrelated (reproduces identically on `main`); `vp lint` passes clean. Added a changeset (`docs-og-locale-metadata.md`)."}

how do I make this svg have a white background?
Add a `<rect>` covering the full `viewBox` as the first child, filled white — SVGs have no background by default, and the `background` attribute you have isn't valid SVG (it's ignored).

Also removed the invalid `fill`/`background` attributes on the `<svg>` root — `fill` there only sets the default fill for child shapes without their own `fill` (harmless but misleading here since both shapes already set their own), and `background` isn't a real SVG attribute at all.
